content.extracted_text:
Percutaneous edge-to-edge mitral valve repair should be considered in carefully selected patients with secondary mitral regurgitation, not eligible for surgery and not needing coronary revascularization, who are symptomatic despite OMT and who fulfil criteria to achieve a reduction in HF hospitalizations.

Percutaneous edge-to-edge mitral valve repair may be considered to improve symptoms in carefully selected patients with secondary mitral regurgitation, not eligible for surgery and not needing coronary revascularization, who are highly symptomatic despite OMT and who do not fulfil criteria for reducing HF hospitalization.

recommendations.recommendation: Percutaneous edge-to-edge mitral valve repair should be considered
recommendations.patient_selection: Carefully selected patients not eligible for surgery, not needing coronary revascularization, symptomatic despite OMT, who fulfil criteria to achieve a reduction in HF hospitalizations
recommendations.notes: Aimed at reducing heart failure (HF) hospitalizations; OMT = optimal medical therapy

recommendations.recommendation: Percutaneous edge-to-edge mitral valve repair may be considered to improve symptoms
recommendations.patient_selection: Carefully selected patients not eligible for surgery, not needing coronary revascularization, highly symptomatic despite OMT, who do not fulfil criteria for reducing HF hospitalization
recommendations.notes: Primarily symptom improvement rather than proven reduction in HF hospitalizations
